# Sprint Plan

## Sprint 1: Review the pull request in pr/

The change under review is `pr/head.diff` (unified diff, base to head). The files before the change are under `pr/base/`, after it under `pr/head/`; `pr/PR.md` is the pull request description and is the implementation report for this sprint.

### Tasks

- [x] Task 1.1: the change in `pr/head.diff`

### Review scope

The gates review `pr/head.diff` (pass `--diff-file pr/head.diff` to the adversarial review). Cite findings as `head/<path>:<line>` with lines from the `pr/head/` files.

## Success Criteria

review the pull request, report each defect it introduces with the file and line it sits on, and give a merge verdict
======
# Task brief

## Criterion

review the pull request, report each defect it introduces with the file and line it sits on, and give a merge verdict

## Task

# Task: review a pull request

The directory `pr/` holds one pull request against a repository of shell scripts, tests and documentation, frozen for evaluation. The change: sprint-259 tasks and seeders (implementers D, E) — sixteen frozen-suite tasks under grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/tasks/ (bugfix-01…04, refactor-01…04 by D: synthetic planted defe….

The pull request is laid out as:

- `pr/PR.md` — the title and description
- `pr/head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base to head)
- `pr/base/` — every touched file before the change
- `pr/head/` — every touched file after the change

Review the change as the senior technical reviewer for the repository: find the defects it introduces and decide whether it can merge. Do not change any file under `pr/`.

## Output contract

Write your review to `review.md` at the repository root (a review workflow that also writes its own report files may do so; `review.md` follows this shape regardless):

- one finding per line, in the form `head/<path>:<line> — <description>`, where `<path>` is the file's path under `pr/head/` and `<line>` is a line number in that file;
- a final line that is exactly `Verdict: APPROVED` or `Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED`.
======
# Audit instructions

This workspace holds one pull request against the Loa framework repository, frozen for evaluation.

- `PR.md` — the PR title and description
- `head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base → head)
- `base/` — every touched file before the change
- `head/` — every touched file after the change

Audit the change as the security auditor for this repository. There is no sprint plan, beads database, implementation report or `grimoires/loa/a2a/` directory here — the PR files above are the entire input; skip any pre-flight step that needs them and do not ask questions.

Write your audit to `audit.md` in this directory using the Write tool. Cite every finding as `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers taken from the `head/` files. Follow your auditor skill's output format and end the file with its machine-readable verdict trailer.
======
# NOTES

## Session Continuity

- 2026-10-21 review-sprint sprint-1 (task review-r23): CHANGES_REQUIRED — 4 high / 8 medium / 9 low; feedback at grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md, task-brief contract copy at review.md. Reproductions live under /tmp/rev (seeder false proof failure with TMPDIR under a repo; grader TypeError on tarfile filter with Python 3.11.2; root conftest.py forging hidden 2/2).

head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:225 — apply_patch falls back to `git apply -p1` when `patch` is absent; from a proof tree under any git work tree (TMPDIR under a checkout) git resolves paths against that repo, prints "Skipped patch" and exits 0, so the seeder reports a false "not green at reference" proof failure (exit 1, nothing written); a non-applying patch is likewise reported as applied
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:714 — `tf.extractall(tree, filter=keep)` needs Python 3.12 or a backport; on Python 3.11.2 every run with a snapshot bundle and a gate verdict dies with "internal error: TypeError: TarFile.extractall() got an unexpected keyword argument 'filter'" (exit 2)
head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:16 — BATS_BIN hard-codes one operator's $HOME dotfiles path; make_bin symlinks $T/bin/bats to it (line 48) and the stub PATH omits /usr/local/bin (line 51), so the bf-sh tests in AG-2/AG-7 fail on any other machine
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:657 — prepare restores/removes only paths listed in grader_protected, and the seeder lists only infrastructure files present at the parent (seed_tasks.py:384); an agent-added root conftest.py (pytest_runtest_makereport hookwrapper) or pytest.ini forges hidden 2/2 with parse_error false
head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:570 — `selected = cands[:select]` fixes the slate before building; a candidate skipped post-selection (no covering test, runner mix, secret refusal) consumes its slot and no later candidate is pulled in, contradicting the wrapper headers ("skipped and does not count")
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1122 — refactor snapshot trees run only test_command; the structural check runs on final alone, so a gate that APPROVED an un-refactored tree is scored accurate
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:864 — envelope_texts emits `anchor` verbatim and file+line only; real dissent envelopes use `anchor: "<path>:<symbol>"` with `anchor_line`, which the CITE regex never matches, so dissent findings add no citation and review-catch recall under-counts
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:977 — ABS_WORD accepts words after `|`, quotes, `=` or `:`; `sed 's|/old/path|/new|'`, `grep '/api/v1'` or `re.sub('/x/y', …)` in a Bash tool call marks a clean run contaminated (outside_path); `"hidden" in low` (line 964) fires on any Grep pattern or file name containing the substring
head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:204 — the proof runs plain `python3 -m pytest` (cwd on sys.path) while the grader rewrites the command with -I/-s or -P and --rootdir (ablation-grade.sh:492-493); tests importing relative to the tree root prove green and grade 0/N, and `-P` fails outright on Python 3.10 (recorded as parse_error, passed 0)
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:296 — copy_tree calls shutil.copyfile on every regular file; a mode-000 file the agent leaves in the sandbox raises PermissionError, caught only as "internal error" (exit 2), so the graded party can veto its grade
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1076 — the final tree copy and churn() include agent-created .venv/node_modules/.tox/.mypy_cache trees and read every differing file whole into memory; diff_lines/files_changed are dominated by dependencies and a large artefact aborts the grade
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:617 — parse_tap keys results by description; repeated @test names across bats files collapse into one key, so failed_names/newly_failing ids are wrong while counts stay right
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1093 — when the final regression run has no parseable summary, newly_failing becomes every base-passing test although run_suite credited passed = total for rc 0 (line 633); the regressions block contradicts itself
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:562 — OUTCOME_RX is applied to every output line; under -rA pytest prints captured output of tests, so a fixture tool printing "FAILED …"/"ERROR <path>" at line start is parsed as an outcome (an ERROR without :: decrements total)
head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:53 — _git_env keeps HOME but does not set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null as the grader does; user log.showSignature/color settings alter the parsed git log and diff output
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1058 — a feedback file without a trailer yields verdict.value "none" (string sentinel, not null) and review.md's Verdict line is then ignored; line 1280 prints Python None in the human summary
head/evals/tests/validate-suite.bats:38 — VS-1 assumes a type whose count differs from four yields exactly one counts: line; a type with more than four tasks may yield none and the expected exit status flips with it
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1175 — `patch` (and `yq`, line 213) are hard prerequisites but unchecked; self-check reference dies with an internal-error FileNotFoundError when patch is absent instead of a usage error
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1045 — grade (98 lines), load_task (319-419) and seed_tasks.py build_bugfix/main exceed the 50-line guideline without justification
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.content:
---
name: audit
description: Security and quality audit of application codebase
role: review
effort: medium
allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, WebFetch, WebSearch, Bash(.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh *), Bash(br sync --import-only), Bash(br sync --flush-only), Bash(br comments add *), Bash(br label add *), Bash(.claude/scripts/beads/log-discovered-issue.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob *)
disallowed-tools:
  - NotebookEdit
capabilities:
  schema_version: 1
  read_files: true
  search_code: true
  write_files: true
  execute_commands:
    allowed:
      - command: ".claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: "br"
        args: ["sync", "--import-only"]
      - command: "br"
        args: ["sync", "--flush-only"]
      - command: "br"
        args: ["comments", "add", "*"]
      - command: "br"
        args: ["label", "add", "*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/beads/log-discovered-issue.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
        args: ["knob", "*"]
    deny_raw_shell: true
  web_access: true
  user_interaction: false
  agent_spawn: false
  task_management: false
cost-profile: heavy
context: fork
parallel_threshold: 2000
audit_categories: 5
timeout_minutes: 60
zones:
  system:
    path: .claude
    permission: none
  state:
    paths: [grimoires/loa, .beads]
    permission: read-write
  app:
    paths: [src, lib, app]

## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`
must equal the review trailer's `excluded`; the golden path refuses to advance otherwise.

**MUST self-check before finishing**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file <audit-output-file> --gate audit --review-file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md`
and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.
</workflow>

Score each dimension 1–5 per `resources/RUBRICS.md` (Security weighted highest; Blockchain when applicable), recording the findings that justify each score.
</rubric_scoring>

</communication_style>

For sprint audits, confirm each task has a documentation-coherence report (Glob `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/documentation-coherence-task-*.md`; sprint level: `documentation-coherence-sprint-*.md`) or was manually verified — checks and red-flag tables: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Documentation. </documentation_audit>

<checklists>
Complete checklists for the five categories (Security, Architecture, Code Quality, DevOps, Blockchain/Crypto): `resources/REFERENCE.md`. Immediate CRITICAL red flags: private keys in code, SQL via string concatenation, user input to eval(), empty catch blocks on security code, hardcoded secrets.

and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`
must equal the review trailer's `excluded`; the golden path refuses to advance otherwise.

**MUST self-check before finishing**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file <audit-output-file> --gate audit --review-file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md`
and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.
</workflow>

<parallel_execution>
## Parallel Splitting (large scopes)

When splitting, use 5 parallel Explore agents — one per category (Security / Architecture / Code Quality / DevOps / Blockchain-Crypto) — each scoped to its category's files and returning findings with severity, file:line, and remediation (per-category file globs and prompts: see `resources/PARALLEL-SPLIT.md`). Consolidate: deduplicate overlaps, sort CRITICAL → LOW, take the overall risk from the highest severity present.
</parallel_execution>

<rubric_scoring>
## Rubric-Based Scoring

Score each dimension 1–5 per `resources/RUBRICS.md` (Security weighted highest; Blockchain when applicable), recording the findings that justify each score.
</rubric_scoring>

<structured_output>
## Structured JSONL Output

Alongside the markdown report, write machine-parseable findings to `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/findings.jsonl` per `resources/OUTPUT-SCHEMA.md` (the schema, each `reasoning_trace`, the closing summary record).
</structured_output>

<communication_style>
Be direct and specific, with evidence: "Line 47: user input passed unsanitized to eval(). Critical RCE. OWASP A03." — never "the code has security issues". Document blast radius, prioritize by exploitability and impact, suggest pragmatic fixes, and never defer a critical issue.
</communication_style>

<documentation_audit>
## Documentation Audit

For sprint audits, confirm each task has a documentation-coherence report (Glob `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/documentation-coherence-task-*.md`; sprint level: `documentation-coherence-sprint-*.md`) or was manually verified — checks and red-flag tables: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Documentation. Blockers: an unverified missing report; uncommented security-critical code; a CHANGELOG omitting security changes; secrets or internal URLs in docs or comments; auth/crypto changes without security documentation; API changes that don't match the endpoint docs.
</documentation_audit>

<checklists>
Complete checklists for the five categories (Security, Architecture, Code Quality, DevOps, Blockchain/Crypto): `resources/REFERENCE.md`. Immediate CRITICAL red flags: private keys in code, SQL via string concatenation, user input to eval(), empty catch blocks on security code, hardcoded secrets.

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (pr/PR.md)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change adds the cycle-130 ablation grader (`evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh`, 1299 lines), the bug-fix and refactor task seeders (`seed-bugfix-tasks.sh`, `seed-refactor-tasks.sh`, `lib/seed_tasks.py`), the generated-path rule for fix regions in `seed-corpus-from-record.sh` (with the pr-14/pr-15 manifests and SHA256SUMS regenerated — checksums verified to match), the `source.churn` schema in `validate-suite.sh`, and bats coverage for all of it. The design is careful: trust boundaries are documented, every path from history or from the sandbox is validated, the grading trees never write into the sandbox, and the seeders prove red/green before a task is moved into place.

I exercised the new code directly rather than relying on the report: syntax checks on every script, the grader against synthetic runs in host mode, and both seeders against throwaway repositories. That surfaced four blocking defects, each reproduced on this host: the seeder's `git apply` fallback silently skips the reference patch when the proof tree sits under any git work tree (so every candidate "fails" its proof), the grader crashes on any run with a snapshot bundle on Python 3.11.2 because `tarfile.extractall(filter=)` is unavailable, the grader's bats suite hard-codes one operator's `$HOME` path for the bats binary, and an agent-authored root `conftest.py` forges a full pass of the hidden tests because the seeder protects only infrastructure files that already exist at the parent commit.

The cross-model dissent (gpt-5.5-pro via codex-headless, companion claude-headless; 2/2 voices, consensus, nothing rejected) returned eight advisory findings; six are real and are folded into the observations below with their own citations. `reviewer.md` is the PR description and carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough; the PR title also names sixteen task directories and "the freeze" that are not in the diff (see Observations).

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Functionality — seeder proof is a false negative without `patch`

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:225-230` — when `patch` is not installed, `apply_patch` runs `git apply -p1` with `cwd=tree`; if the proof tree lies anywhere under a git work tree (the seeder builds it with `tempfile.mkdtemp`, so any `TMPDIR` under a checkout — here `TMPDIR=/workspace/.eval/tmp`), git resolves patch paths against that repository's root, prints `Skipped patch 'tools/mathx/rounding.py'.` and exits 0. The seeder treats that as applied, runs the reference tests on the unpatched tree and reports `proof-failed <sha>: not green at reference (exit 1, 2 failed, 1 passed)`, exits 1 and writes nothing.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:225-230`
**Issue:** Reproduced with the SB-1 repository from `seed-bugfix.bats`: with `TMPDIR` under `/workspace` the run fails as above; with `TMPDIR=/tmp/rev/tmp` the same run prints `proof bugfix-01 …: red 2 failed / green 3 passed` and writes the task. A controlled check from a subdirectory of an unrelated repository showed `git apply` returning 0 with the file unchanged. The inverse also holds: a reference patch that does not apply is reported as applied.
**Why This Matters:** The whole point of the seeder is the red/green proof. On a host without `patch` (as this one) the proof's outcome depends on where `TMPDIR` points, and the failure mode is silent: every candidate is rejected and the operator sees "proof failed", not "patch skipped".
**Required Fix:** Either require `patch` in the wrappers' tool check (`seed-bugfix-tasks.sh:75`, `seed-refactor-tasks.sh:64`), as the grader's self-check already does implicitly, or make the fallback safe: run `git apply` with `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` set to the parent of the proof tree (or `git -C tree init -q` the scratch tree first), and treat any `Skipped patch` line on stderr as failure.
**Reference:** git-apply(1) — "When running from a subdirectory in a repository, patched paths outside the directory are ignored."

### 2. Functionality — grader aborts on Python without the tarfile extraction filter

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:713-714` — `tf.extractall(tree, filter=keep)` requires Python 3.12, or the 3.11.4/3.10.12/3.9.17/3.8.17 backports. On this host (Python 3.11.2, `hasattr(tarfile, "data_filter")` is False) every grade of a run that has a snapshot bundle and a gate verdict dies with `ablation-grade: internal error: TypeError: TarFile.extractall() got an unexpected keyword argument 'filter'` and exit 2.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:713-714`
**Issue:** Reproduced with a synthetic bug-fix run in host mode: without a snapshot the grade succeeds (`hidden 0/2`); after adding `snapshots/IMPLEMENT.bundle`, `index.json` and a review trailer the grader exits 2. That is exactly the shape of every A1-arm run (REVIEW ran, so `implement` is graded), so `ablation-grade.bats` AG-6, AG-12 and AG-18 fail here too. The grader is the host-side component (it is what `python3 -I -` on the operator host runs), so the image's Python does not help.
**Why This Matters:** The grader hard-depends on an interpreter feature without checking for it, and the result is not a degraded grade but no grade.
**Required Fix:** Guard the call: when `tarfile.data_filter` exists use it; otherwise pre-filter members with the same `safe_rel`/`EXCLUDE_TOP` checks plus explicit rejections of absolute names, `..`, links, devices and members whose realpath lands outside `tree`, and pass them via `members=`. Alternatively pin the minimum Python in the header and fail fast with a `GradeError` naming it.
**Reference:** CWE-22 (the filter is the path-traversal defence; the fallback must keep it), Python docs tarfile "Extraction filters".

### 3. Testing — the grader's bats suite runs only on the author's machine

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:16` — `BATS_BIN="$HOME/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats"` hard-codes one operator's dotfiles path; `make_bin` symlinks `$T/bin/bats` to it (line 48) and the docker stub's PATH is `$T/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` (line 51), which omits `/usr/local/bin`. On any other host the symlink dangles and bats-core installed under `/usr/local/bin` (as here) is not found: the `bf-sh` halves of AG-2 and AG-7 fail (`bats: command not found` → rc 127 → `parse_error`, `passed 0`).
**File:** `head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:16`
**Issue:** The only tests of the 1299-line grader cannot run in CI or on a colleague's machine; a reviewer re-running them gets red for reasons unrelated to the grader.
**Why This Matters:** FAST-GATE parity: a test file that only passes locally is equivalent to an unrun test.
**Required Fix:** Resolve bats from PATH (`command -v bats`), honour `LOA_SEED_BATS` like the seeder does, and `skip` when neither resolves; include the resolved binary's directory in `DOCKER_STUB_PATH`.

### 4. Grading integrity — unprotected pytest configuration lets the graded tree forge its hidden-test result

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:657-674` — `prepare` restores or removes only the paths listed in `grader_protected`; everything else in the agent's tree is run as-is, and pytest loads any `conftest.py` (and `pytest.ini`/`pyproject.toml`/`setup.cfg`/`tox.ini`) it finds from the rootdir down. The seeder writes `grader_protected` from `helper_files` (`head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:158-177`, `:384`), which lists only infrastructure files that EXIST at the parent commit, so a root `conftest.py` or ini file the fixture lacks is never removed from the graded tree.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:657-674` (and `head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:384`)
**Issue:** Reproduced in host mode on a seeded-shape task (`grader_protected: [tests/conftest.py]`): the fixture alone grades `hidden 0/2`; adding a root `conftest.py` with a `pytest_runtest_makereport` hookwrapper that sets `rep.outcome = "passed"` grades `hidden 2/2, parse_error false` with no change to the source. A root `pytest.ini` with `addopts` is the same vector. Agents add root `conftest.py` files routinely (import-path fixes), so this is not only an adversarial path.
**Why This Matters:** `hidden_tests.passed/total` is the primary build metric of the ablation; an unprotected hook makes it agent-controlled while the grade reports a clean parse.
**Required Fix:** In the seeder, always list the standard pytest configuration paths (root `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, `tox.ini`, and `conftest.py` in every test directory of `test_command`) in `grader_protected` even when absent, so `prepare` removes agent-added copies; have `validate-suite.sh` require them for pytest tasks; in the grader, additionally pass `-c /dev/null` (no ini from the tree) and `-p no:cacheprovider --confcutdir=<rootdir>` only if the task's own conftests remain loadable, or document that `grader_protected` is the sole defence and audit the sixteen frozen tasks for it.
**Reference:** CWE-807 (reliance on untrusted inputs in a security decision), pytest docs "conftest.py: local per-directory plugins".

---

## Observations

### 1. Seeder selection contract

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:570-602` — `selected = cands[: a.select]` fixes the slate before building; a candidate that is skipped after selection (`no test at the parent names a touched file`, the covering-tests runner mix, a secret refusal) consumes its slot and no later candidate is pulled in. Reproduced: two refactor candidates, the newest without a covering test, `--select 1` → `selected 1, written 0`, exit 0, although `--select 2` writes the older one. The wrapper headers promise the opposite (`seed-refactor-tasks.sh:37-38`, `seed-bugfix-tasks.sh:43-44`).
**Suggestion:** Iterate over all candidates and stop when `written + failed == select`.
**Benefit:** `--select 4` yields four tasks when four qualify.

### 2. Refactor gates are judged without the structural check (dissent DISS-002)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1122` — snapshot trees run only `t.test_command`; `structural_command(t)` runs on `final` alone (line 1101). For a refactor whose functional suite is green at base, an unchanged IMPLEMENT snapshot passes everything the gate is judged on, so a review that APPROVED the un-refactored tree gets `verdict_accuracy_per_gate.review: true` (line 1129-1130).
**Suggestion:** For refactor tasks run the structural check on each graded snapshot and require both to pass in `all_pass`.
**Benefit:** Gate accuracy measures what the task asked for.

### 3. Dissent envelopes contribute no citations (dissent DISS-001, DISS-C-006)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:854-868` — `envelope_texts` emits `anchor` verbatim and `file`+`line`, but the adversarial envelopes the harness copies under `eval/` use `anchor: "<path>:<symbol>"` with `anchor_line`/`anchor_line_end` (this sprint's own `adversarial-review.json` is an example; AG-8 only exercises `anchor: "lib/x.sh:20"` and `file`/`line`). The `CITE` regex needs `:digits`, so real dissent findings never reach `gates-combined.md`, and recall under-counts arms where the dissent is what caught the defect, contrary to the header (lines 96-97).
**Suggestion:** When `anchor_line` is an int, split `anchor` at the first `:` and emit `path:anchor_line[-anchor_line_end]`.
**Benefit:** Review-catch recall credits the gate the design says it credits.

### 4. Contamination false positives on quoted slash strings (dissent DISS-C-003)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:976-980` — `ABS_WORD` accepts a word preceded by `|`, `'`, `"`, `=` or `:`; checked here: `re.sub('/x/y', …)` yields `/x/y`. So `sed 's|/old/path|/new|'`, `grep '/api/v1'` or `echo "/a/b"` in any Bash tool call marks the run `contaminated: outside_path` on the first such command, and `"hidden" in low` (line 964) fires on a Grep pattern or a file name containing the substring. The header calls the scan a lower bound on leakage, but these are false positives that flag clean runs.
**Suggestion:** Only consider Bash words that are bare argv tokens (not inside quotes or sed/grep delimiters), and require a known top-level prefix (`/home`, `/root`, `/mnt`, `/srv`, `/media`, `/run`) for `outside_path`; scope `hidden` to path fields and words that resolve under the task directory.
**Benefit:** Arm comparisons are not biased by shell style.

### 5. The seeder proves under a different interpreter shape than the grader runs (dissent DISS-C-002)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:201-210` vs `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:492-493` — the proof runs plain `python3 -m pytest` (cwd on `sys.path`); the grader rewrites the same command as `python3 -I -s` (container) or `python3 -P` (host) with `--rootdir`, removing the cwd entry. Tests that import fixture modules relative to the tree root pass the seeding proof and grade 0/N. `-P` also needs Python 3.11; on a 3.10 host every host-mode pytest run exits 2 (`Unknown option: -P`) and is recorded as `parse_error`, `passed 0`, not as a tool failure.
**Suggestion:** Share `shape_command` between seeder and grader (move it to `lib/`) so the proof uses the graded argv; treat rc 2 with no collected tests as a `GradeError`.
**Benefit:** A task that proves green cannot grade red for reasons unrelated to the agent.

### 6. An unreadable file in the sandbox aborts the grade

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:296` — `copy_tree` calls `shutil.copyfile` on every regular file; a mode-000 file the agent leaves behind raises `PermissionError`, caught only by the generic handler: `internal error: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: …/sandbox/blocker.txt`, exit 2. Reproduced as uid 1000. `churn` already tolerates this (line 731-734); `copy_tree` does not.
**Suggestion:** Catch `OSError` per file, skip it and record the count in grade.json (or chmod the copy source as `remove_path` does for directories).
**Benefit:** The graded party cannot veto its own grade.

### 7. Churn and the final tree include dependency and build trees (dissent DISS-C-005)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1076-1077` and `:719-757` — only a fixed top-level list and `__pycache__`/`.pytest_cache` are excluded; a `.venv`, `node_modules`, `.tox` or `.mypy_cache` the agent created is copied into `grading/final`, counted in `files_changed`/`diff_lines`, and read whole into memory for `difflib`. `diff_lines` is a cross-arm metric.
**Suggestion:** Extend `EXCLUDE_ANY` with the usual dependency/build/cache directories (or honour the sandbox `.gitignore`), cap the per-file size for line diffs, and count larger files as 1 file / 0 lines.
**Benefit:** Churn measures the agent's edits.

### 8. Report and scope

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/../pr/PR.md:1` — the title says "sixteen frozen-suite tasks under grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/tasks/" and the second commit "the grader, the freeze and bd-8o5rx", yet the diff holds no task directory, no `MANIFEST.sha256` and no `freeze.sh` change (16 files: harness, tests, fixtures). `reviewer.md` carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough and no record of the test commands run. VS-1 was rewritten to count whatever is committed (`head/evals/tests/validate-suite.bats:31-45`), so nothing in this PR pins the sixteen tasks' existence or validity.
**Suggestion:** Either include the task directories and the freeze in this change or drop them from the description; add the AC walkthrough with `file:line` evidence and the bats/pytest commands that were run.
**Benefit:** The review can check what the PR claims.

### 9. Lower-severity notes

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:617-621` — `parse_tap` keys results by description; two `@test` names repeated across bats files collapse into one key, so `failed_names`/`newly_failing` ids are wrong while counts stay right (dissent DISS-C-004). Key by test number.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1091-1095` — when the final regression run has no parseable summary, `newly_failing` becomes every base-passing test even though `run_suite` credited `passed = total` for rc 0 (line 633); the regressions block contradicts itself (dissent DISS-C-007). Surface `parse_error` in the block and only derive `newly` from rc.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:561-571` — `OUTCOME_RX` is applied to every output line; under `-rA` pytest prints captured stdout of passed and failed tests, so a fixture tool printing `FAILED …`/`ERROR <path>` at line start is parsed as an outcome (an `ERROR` without `::` even decrements `total`) (dissent DISS-C-001). Scan only the "short test summary info" section.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:51-54` — `_git_env` keeps `HOME` but does not set `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` as the grader does (`ablation-grade.sh:679`); a user `log.showSignature` or `color.ui=always` changes the parsed `git log`/`diff` output.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1057-1063` — a feedback file without a trailer yields `verdict.value: "none"` (a string sentinel) and `review.md`'s `Verdict:` line is then not consulted; the header describes `value` as the verdict or null. Line 1280 also prints Python's `None` in the human summary.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/tests/validate-suite.bats:35-45` — VS-1 assumes a type with a count other than four produces exactly one `counts:` line; a type with more than four tasks may produce none, and the expected status flips with it.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:213` and `:1175` — `yq` and `patch` are hard prerequisites (self-check reference dies with an `internal error` `FileNotFoundError` when `patch` is absent, as here) but neither the header's prerequisites nor a pre-flight check names them; the wrappers check only `git`/`python3`.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1045-1142` — complexity: `grade` (98 lines), `load_task` (`:319-419`, 101 lines), `build_bugfix` (`seed_tasks.py:370-436`) and `main` (`seed_tasks.py:547-620`) exceed the 50-line guideline without a justification comment; splitting `grade` into build/review-catch halves would also make the refactor-snapshot fix above local. `SIMPLICITY[shrink]`: otherwise lean; no over-engineering found. `Lean already. Ship.` once the above is addressed.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) no CHANGELOG entry is part of the diff for the new grader, seeders or the schema change; add one per the repository's documentation rule.

### Cross-Model Observations

Both voices returned advisory findings only. DISS-002, DISS-C-001, DISS-C-002, DISS-C-003, DISS-C-004, DISS-C-005, DISS-C-006 and DISS-C-007 are triaged above (Observations 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 9). DISS-001 duplicates DISS-C-006. No dissent finding was discarded.

## Rejected dissent payloads

None: `metadata.rejected_summary` is empty and the sidecar `adversarial-rejected-review.jsonl` holds no rows.

---

## Acceptance Criteria Check

### Task 1.1: the change in `pr/head.diff`

| Criterion (from the files' own headers) | Status | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Seeder: task built in a private dir, moved only after red/green proof and no-secrets pass | Fail | Proof is a false negative when `patch` is absent and TMPDIR is under a repo (Changes Required 1); otherwise verified end to end on a throwaway repo (task.yaml, TASK.md, fixture contents match SB-1's expectations) |

**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md

---

## Overall Assessment

The change adds the cycle-130 ablation grader (`evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh`, 1299 lines), the bug-fix and refactor task seeders (`seed-bugfix-tasks.sh`, `seed-refactor-tasks.sh`, `lib/seed_tasks.py`), the generated-path rule for fix regions in `seed-corpus-from-record.sh` (with the pr-14/pr-15 manifests and SHA256SUMS regenerated — checksums verified to match), the `source.churn` schema in `validate-suite.sh`, and bats coverage for all of it. The design is careful: trust boundaries are documented, every path from history or from the sandbox is validated, the grading trees never write into the sandbox, and the seeders prove red/green before a task is moved into place.

I exercised the new code directly rather than relying on the report: syntax checks on every script, the grader against synthetic runs in host mode, and both seeders against throwaway repositories. That surfaced four blocking defects, each reproduced on this host: the seeder's `git apply` fallback silently skips the reference patch when the proof tree sits under any git work tree (so every candidate "fails" its proof), the grader crashes on any run with a snapshot bundle on Python 3.11.2 because `tarfile.extractall(filter=)` is unavailable, the grader's bats suite hard-codes one operator's `$HOME` path for the bats binary, and an agent-authored root `conftest.py` forges a full pass of the hidden tests because the seeder protects only infrastructure files that already exist at the parent commit.

The cross-model dissent (gpt-5.5-pro via codex-headless, companion claude-headless; 2/2 voices, consensus, nothing rejected) returned eight advisory findings; six are real and are folded into the observations below with their own citations. `reviewer.md` is the PR description and carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough; the PR title also names sixteen task directories and "the freeze" that are not in the diff (see Observations).

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Functionality — seeder proof is a false negative without `patch`

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:225-230` — when `patch` is not installed, `apply_patch` runs `git apply -p1` with `cwd=tree`; if the proof tree lies anywhere under a git work tree (the seeder builds it with `tempfile.mkdtemp`, so any `TMPDIR` under a checkout — here `TMPDIR=/workspace/.eval/tmp`), git resolves patch paths against that repository's root, prints `Skipped patch 'tools/mathx/rounding.py'.` and exits 0. The seeder treats that as applied, runs the reference tests on the unpatched tree and reports `proof-failed <sha>: not green at reference (exit 1, 2 failed, 1 passed)`, exits 1 and writes nothing.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:225-230`
**Issue:** Reproduced with the SB-1 repository from `seed-bugfix.bats`: with `TMPDIR` under `/workspace` the run fails as above; with `TMPDIR=/tmp/rev/tmp` the same run prints `proof bugfix-01 …: red 2 failed / green 3 passed` and writes the task. A controlled check from a subdirectory of an unrelated repository showed `git apply` returning 0 with the file unchanged. The inverse also holds: a reference patch that does not apply is reported as applied.
**Why This Matters:** The whole point of the seeder is the red/green proof. On a host without `patch` (as this one) the proof's outcome depends on where `TMPDIR` points, and the failure mode is silent: every candidate is rejected and the operator sees "proof failed", not "patch skipped".
**Required Fix:** Either require `patch` in the wrappers' tool check (`seed-bugfix-tasks.sh:75`, `seed-refactor-tasks.sh:64`), as the grader's self-check already does implicitly, or make the fallback safe: run `git apply` with `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` set to the parent of the proof tree (or `git -C tree init -q` the scratch tree first), and treat any `Skipped patch` line on stderr as failure.
**Reference:** git-apply(1) — "When running from a subdirectory in a repository, patched paths outside the directory are ignored."

### 2. Functionality — grader aborts on Python without the tarfile extraction filter

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:713-714` — `tf.extractall(tree, filter=keep)` requires Python 3.12, or the 3.11.4/3.10.12/3.9.17/3.8.17 backports. **File:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:713-714`
**Issue:** Reproduced with a synthetic bug-fix run in host mode: without a snapshot the grade succeeds (`hidden 0/2`); after adding `snapshots/IMPLEMENT.bundle`, `index.json` and a review trailer the grader exits 2. That is exactly the shape of every A1-arm run (REVIEW ran, so `implement` is graded), so `ablation-grade.bats` AG-6, AG-12 and AG-18 fail here too. The grader is the host-side component (it is what `python3 -I -` on the operator host runs), so the image's Python does not help.
**Why This Matters:** The grader hard-depends on an interpreter feature without checking for it, and the result is not a degraded grade but no grade.
**Required Fix:** Guard the call: when `tarfile.data_filter` exists use it; otherwise pre-filter members with the same `safe_rel`/`EXCLUDE_TOP` checks plus explicit rejections of absolute names, `..`, links, devices and members whose realpath lands outside `tree`, and pass them via `members=`. Alternatively pin the minimum Python in the header and fail fast with a `GradeError` naming it.
**Reference:** CWE-22 (the filter is the path-traversal defence; the fallback must keep it), Python docs tarfile "Extraction filters".

### 3. Testing — the grader's bats suite runs only on the author's machine

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:16` — `BATS_BIN="$HOME/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats"` hard-codes one operator's dotfiles path; `make_bin` symlinks `$T/bin/bats` to it (line 48) and the docker stub's PATH is `$T/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` (line 51), which omits `/usr/local/bin`. **File:** `head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:16`
**Issue:** The only tests of the 1299-line grader cannot run in CI or on a colleague's machine; a reviewer re-running them gets red for reasons unrelated to the grader.
**Why This Matters:** FAST-GATE parity: a test file that only passes locally is equivalent to an unrun test.
**Required Fix:** Resolve bats from PATH (`command -v bats`), honour `LOA_SEED_BATS` like the seeder does, and `skip` when neither resolves; include the resolved binary's directory in `DOCKER_STUB_PATH`.

### 4. Grading integrity — unprotected pytest configuration lets the graded tree forge its hidden-test result

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:657-674` — `prepare` restores or removes only the paths listed in `grader_protected`; everything else in the agent's tree is run as-is, and pytest loads any `conftest.py` (and `pytest.ini`/`pyproject.toml`/`setup.cfg`/`tox.ini`) it finds from the rootdir down. **Issue:** Reproduced in host mode on a seeded-shape task (`grader_protected: [tests/conftest.py]`): the fixture alone grades `hidden 0/2`; adding a root `conftest.py` with a `pytest_runtest_makereport` hookwrapper that sets `rep.outcome = "passed"` grades `hidden 2/2, parse_error false` with no change to the source. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Security Audit Scope Analysis
# Two-Pass Methodology v1.0
#
# Shows file counts by security-relevant category to understand audit surface.
# Part of Loa's /audit skill enhancement.
#
# Usage: .claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh [OPTIONS]
#   --no-symlinks    Skip symlinks (default: follow)
#   --max-depth N    Limit search depth (default: unlimited)
#   --json           Output as JSON

set -euo pipefail

# Parse arguments
FOLLOW_SYMLINKS=true
MAX_DEPTH=""
OUTPUT_JSON=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case $1 in
    --no-symlinks) FOLLOW_SYMLINKS=false; shift ;;
    --max-depth) MAX_DEPTH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json) OUTPUT_JSON=true; shift ;;
    *) echo "Unknown option: $1"; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

# Build find options as array (HIGH-002 remediation - prevents word splitting)
declare -a FIND_OPTS=(-type f)
if [[ "$FOLLOW_SYMLINKS" == "false" ]]; then
  FIND_OPTS=(-type f -not -type l)
fi
if [[ -n "$MAX_DEPTH" ]]; then
  FIND_OPTS=(-maxdepth "$MAX_DEPTH" "${FIND_OPTS[@]}")
fi

# Exclude patterns (POSIX compatible)
EXCLUDE_DIRS="node_modules|\.git|dist|build|\.next|vendor|__pycache__|\.venv"

# Count function with error suppression
# Uses array expansion for safe variable handling
count_files() {
  local pattern="$1"
  local result
  result=$(find . "${FIND_OPTS[@]}" \( -name "*.ts" -o -name "*.js" -o -name "*.py" -o -name "*.go" -o -name "*.java" \) 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -v -E "$EXCLUDE_DIRS" | \
    xargs grep -l "$pattern" 2>/dev/null | wc -l || echo "0")
  echo "$result" | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

count_by_name() {
  local pattern="$1"
  local result
  result=$(find . "${FIND_OPTS[@]}" \( -name "*$pattern*" \) 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -v -E "$EXCLUDE_DIRS" | wc -l || echo "0")
  echo "$result" | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Security Audit Scope Analysis
# Two-Pass Methodology v1.0
#
# Shows file counts by security-relevant category to understand audit surface.
# Part of Loa's /audit skill enhancement.
#
# Usage: .claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh [OPTIONS]
#   --no-symlinks    Skip symlinks (default: follow)
#   --max-depth N    Limit search depth (default: unlimited)
#   --json           Output as JSON

set -euo pipefail

# Parse arguments
FOLLOW_SYMLINKS=true
MAX_DEPTH=""
OUTPUT_JSON=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case $1 in
    --no-symlinks) FOLLOW_SYMLINKS=false; shift ;;
    --max-depth) MAX_DEPTH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json) OUTPUT_JSON=true; shift ;;
    *) echo "Unknown option: $1"; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

# Build find options as array (HIGH-002 remediation - prevents word splitting)
declare -a FIND_OPTS=(-type f)
if [[ "$FOLLOW_SYMLINKS" == "false" ]]; then
  FIND_OPTS=(-type f -not -type l)
fi
if [[ -n "$MAX_DEPTH" ]]; then
  FIND_OPTS=(-maxdepth "$MAX_DEPTH" "${FIND_OPTS[@]}")
fi

# Exclude patterns (POSIX compatible)
EXCLUDE_DIRS="node_modules|\.git|dist|build|\.next|vendor|__pycache__|\.venv"

# Count function with error suppression
# Uses array expansion for safe variable handling
count_files() {
  local pattern="$1"
  local result
  result=$(find . "${FIND_OPTS[@]}" \( -name "*.ts" -o -name "*.js" -o -name "*.py" -o -name "*.go" -o -name "*.java" \) 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -v -E "$EXCLUDE_DIRS" | \
    xargs grep -l "$pattern" 2>/dev/null | wc -l || echo "0")
  echo "$result" | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

count_by_name() {
  local pattern="$1"
  local result
  result=$(find . "${FIND_OPTS[@]}" \( -name "*$pattern*" \) 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -v -E "$EXCLUDE_DIRS" | wc -l || echo "0")
  echo "$result" | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

## Independence

The dissenter receives the diff only — never `--context-file` with your Phase 1A/1B findings —
so it evaluates the code without anchoring on your conclusions.

## Merging dissenter findings into Phase 2

1. CRITICAL/HIGH findings go into the audit report as findings of your own (they may change the
   verdict and must appear in the Phase 2.5 tally).
2. MEDIUM/LOW findings go under a "Cross-Model Security Observations" section.
3. A dissenter finding that duplicates one of yours is marked "Confirmed by cross-model review".

## Failed or unavailable dissenter

Output file: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`. The
`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.

Then set a `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker in the audit report. Empty

## Two voices and the rejected-payload contract (cycle-126 FR-2)

**Companion voice (D-2.1).** Every dissent plans a second chain from the *other* provider
family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,
Google, xAI, unknown) gets the Anthropic chain (`opus` → `claude-headless`), an Anthropic-family primary gets the OpenAI chain
(`gpt-5.5` → `codex-headless`; KF-002 keeps `gpt-5.5-pro` out of the default). Credential *presence* (env → `.env.local` →
`.env`; the value is never read) decides only where the companion chain starts — with no key it
starts at the CLI hop. Both chains walk in parallel; the two completed envelopes are aggregated
(`verdict_quality.voices_succeeded_ids` lists only completed voices). `companion_voice.status` is `succeeded`,
`failed` or `fold_failed`; `verdict_quality.voices_planned` counts the aggregated envelopes — 2 whenever the companion ran,
completed or not (a failed one is listed in `voices_dropped`) — except a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's
succeeded voices: INV-5 lets it feed no envelope, so `voices_planned` stays 1 and `companion_voice` is its only record; a `duplicate_voice` companion contributes none, and a
dropped entry naming the model the companion answered with is removed (INV-5). `companion_voice.counted_as`
(`independent_voice`, `duplicate_voice`, `sole_voice` — the primary never answered) names the outcome, and `planned: false` with a `reason` (`no_workdir`, `no_route`,
`prompt_copy_failed`) is a companion that never started; a bare `planned: false` is the opt-out. The
companion's findings arrive re-numbered `DISS-C-NNN` with a `voice` field; the primary's carry
`voice` too. `metadata.companion_voice` records `{planned, family, family_basis, chain, model,
status: succeeded|failed|fold_failed, failure_class: auth|model_unavailable|quota|timeout|lock_wait|malformed|null,
cost_cents, attempts}`; a companion whose chain fails is a dropped voice (degraded for an audit,
never blocking a review). Opt-out per block: `flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice: false`
(the YAML boolean spellings in any case; a value that is none of them is reported and the voice stays on).

**Tolerant schema (D-2.2).** A finding missing only `failure_mode` is no longer dropped: the
first sentence of its `description` (≤ 200 chars) becomes `failure_mode` and the finding is
marked `failure_mode_derived: true` (a missing `id` is filled positionally, `id_derived: true`).
Severity, category and description are never touched. Payloads that still fail go to the
sidecar (`adversarial-rejected-<type>.jsonl`, `-companion` suffix for the second voice) **and**
to `metadata.rejected_summary[]` as `{index, severity, title, title_derived, anchor, reason, description_head}`.

**The contract (D-2.3).** When `rejected_summary` is non-empty the feedback file MUST contain a
`## Rejected dissent payloads` section with one line per entry — `- <title> (<severity>, <anchor>)
— <reason>: triaged as <real defect → counted under the matching heading | not a defect → why>`.
`verdict-derive.sh` reads the sibling envelope (`adversarial-<gate>.json`, or `--envelope <path>`)
and marks the trailer INCONSISTENT (exit 1) when the section is missing. Reading a sidecar row:
`payload` is the model's finding as normalised, `reject_reason` the clause it failed, and
`repair_attempted` / `repair_succeeded` whether the bounded repair round-trip ran.

**Round-1 hardening (sprint-248 review, sixteen live two-voice runs).** One list, by envelope field; both skills' copies of
this block are kept byte-identical (CMP-138 fails on any drift).

- **Two voices, one envelope.** The companion runs in its own sub-workdir with a log and its own copies of the prompt files.
  The envelope's `cost_usd` / tokens are BOTH voices; the per-voice spend stays under `companion_voice.cost_cents`, and
  `budget_cents` is a per-voice cap (a malformed cap is 0 cents — the run fails closed with `status: budget_exceeded`).
  Findings carry `voice` (the outer hop, matching `final_model`) and `answered_by` (the model that produced them);
  `companion_voice.answered_by` is the companion's own succeeded id. An operator may set
  `flatline_protocol.<block>.companion_chain: {anthropic: [...], openai: [...]}` to replace the default chains of D-2.1

  process.
- **`companion_voice.independent` / `counted_as`.** Independence compares the two `answered_by` families (the primary's
  succeeded id, not its configured hop). Same family — or either family `unknown`, an id no catalog entry or name rule
  places, which is no evidence of a second family: the companion's findings are kept (tagged) but its envelope
  contributes no voice to verdict quality — `counted_as: duplicate_voice` (the aggregator counts distinct voices; its

  dropped entry is aggregated — `primary_attempts_rewritten` / `companion_attempts_rewritten`; an envelope with no
  succeeded voice that dropped the other side's voice is excluded — `primary_attempts_excluded` /
  `companion_attempts_excluded`). A primary that never answered leaves the companion `counted_as: sole_voice`
  (`independent: null`). A primary chain that exhausts while the companion completes is promoted (`status: reviewed`,
  `degraded: true`, `primary_voice: {status: failed}`) so the completed voice is never buried. An aggregator failure is
  named on the envelope (`verdict_quality_error`). A fold that fails keeps the primary envelope
  (`companion_voice.status: fold_failed`) and counts the companion as a dropped voice.
- **Shared hops (`companion_voice.shared_hops`, `primary_voice.status: ceded`).** A hop both chains hold (typically the
  other family's CLI as the primary's last resort) stays in the companion chain and is listed under `shared_hops`,
  compared by canonical name (a provider prefix or a catalog alias is the same hop). When the primary reaches a shared hop
  it waits for the companion to settle (bounded by the wait cap) and skips the hop only when the companion ANSWERED with
  it — `model_attempts` records `<hop>:skipped_shared_with_companion` and the envelope says `primary_voice: {status:

  companion still ON the hop past the wait cap is reaped where the primary stands and the primary runs the hop; a
  companion that already answered and is finishing (its post phase) is left to the post budget. The binary is never run
  twice for the same prompt.

  silent whatever its age: its rows count toward the section and a warning names the file (newer than the envelope: the
  envelope may be stale — re-run; older: an earlier run's rows that were never folded — triage them or remove the file; a

  primary's wait on a shared hop applies the same model (a companion in `post` on another hop frees the hop at once; on

  start (`.prev`) and never restored — see "Rejected rows". Every

  without a leading zero, or its default applies with a warning — except `budget_cents` / `--budget`, which fail closed

  `lock_wait` — no request was sent (the chain walks on); a model that merely resolves to a CLI hop, and a repair, wait only their own call
  timeout; queueing for the lock is not charged to the hop's cap; without `flock` (or a lock directory that is not ours)
  the serialisation is off and said once per run. The queue is one hop deep by design: a chunk driver runs dissents
  sequentially when any chain holds a `*-headless` hop. The envelope `adversarial-<gate>.json` and the two sidecars are
  single-writer per (sprint, gate) — the tag scopes the sidecar names only, never the envelope — so a second live run for
  the same sprint and gate is refused before it removes anything (`status: refused_concurrent_run` under `--json`; a
  dead run's lock is taken over; the token is the acquiring pid and its start time; a lock directory with no token yet is a
  holder in flight for `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_RUN_LOCK_GRACE_SECONDS`, default 5). A diff that prepares to no content is refused
  before the run lock (`status: nothing_to_review` under `--json`, exit 1, no call made); a top-priority file not even one
  hunk of which fits the budget is sent as its PARTIAL marker alone (`0 of N hunks shown`).
- **`failure_class` and `last_error`.** The class follows cheval's exit codes — 4 (`MISSING_API_KEY`) `auth`; 6
  (`BUDGET_EXCEEDED` / `RATE_LIMITED`) or a diagnostic saying "rate limit" / "429" / "quota" `quota`; 3 / 124 `timeout`,
  and a diagnostic saying "timed out" (cheval reports its own CLI-hop timeout as `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`) too; 5
  (`INVALID_RESPONSE`) or a `malformed_response` status `malformed`; anything else (1: API error, provider unavailable,
  token revoked) `model_unavailable`; a hop whose CLI lock was never acquired is `lock_wait` (no request was sent).
  `last_error` is an allowlisted summary of the provider's own line — cheval's error
  tokens, "timed out after Ns", HTTP / exit codes — read from the MODELINV ledger row cheval wrote for the call (the
  model-adapter shim discards cheval's stderr; the row is matched by model, primitive and the window of the companion's
  LAST hop, so a repair on the same model during its post phase is not its row; concurrent dissents on one host could still
  supply each other's line — another reason drivers run sequentially), else from the last non-banner line of the
  companion's log; it also masks bare provider-key shapes (`sk-…`, `xai-…`, `gsk_…`, `AIza…`) the shared redactor does not
  cover. The redacted raw line is printed to stderr and stays in the `/tmp` workdir, removed on exit; the a2a directory
  receives the envelope and the sidecars.
- **Repairs (`repair_hops_skipped`, `repair_budget_exhausted`).** The repair round-trip walks `tiny` (with an Anthropic
  credential) → `claude-headless` (with the binary on PATH) → the voice that answered, always last, one bounded attempt
  each (by canonical name: a prefixed answering voice is not appended twice); a hop that failed with an explicit auth /
  quota code is retired for the run's remaining repairs, the answering voice never; a repair skips a hop the companion is
  running at that moment (`repair_hops_skipped` names it, once) and waits for a CLI lock only its own timeout (a hop
  whose wait expires never ran: named `<hop>:lock_wait`, once, and no repair slot is spent); the run's
  repairs share a wall-clock budget (`LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_BUDGET_SECONDS`, default 5 × timeout × 2 or twice the heaviest hop's charge
  (below) plus a timeout if that is more; a hop whose estimate — twice its last observed duration, at least the timeout,
  at most its bound — exceeds what is left is not started and is named `<hop>:over_budget`; spent, the rest are rejected
  unrepaired and counted in `repair_budget_exhausted`, a payload none of whose hops started for want of budget among them;
  one none of whose hops started for any other reason — every hop retired or being run by the companion — is counted in
  `repair_skipped_no_hop`). `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL` is filtered by the retired hops too. A hop is charged by what it
  can reach, in the repair budget and the companion's post budget alike: a `*-headless` hop its CLI bound, an HTTP alias
  whose chain falls through to a CLI its lock wait, its timeout and that CLI's bound. A derived
  finding id never collides with one the model supplied; the normaliser's `id_derived` / `failure_mode_derived` markers are
  not part of the repair's byte-diff; a derived `failure_mode` shorter than 20 characters (an enumerator, an abbreviation)
  gives way to the description's 200-character head (counted in characters, never bytes).
- **Credentials and ledgers.** Presence resolves per alias with override precedence (env → `.env.local` → `.env`: the
  first place that assigns a variable decides it, an empty assignment disables that alias; a provider with several
  aliases — `GOOGLE_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` — is present when any alias resolves non-empty; the value is never
  expanded). Both cheval invocations append to `.run/cost-ledger.jsonl` and `.run/model-invoke.jsonl` under the writers'
  flock (issue #689), so the hash chain stays linear.

**Repair loop (D-2.4).** The repair chain is `tiny` (when an Anthropic credential is present) →
`claude-headless` (when the binary is on PATH) → the voice that answered, always last — one bounded
attempt per hop, so a host with neither still repairs through its own primary; `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL`
pins the whole chain to one model (the round-1 hardening above has the retirement, lock and budget rules).
KF-004 evidence: the three real rejected payloads under `tests/fixtures/dissent-rejected/` now pass without a repair.

## Numeric anchors and the budget scaling (cycle-131 FR-4)

- **Numeric anchors (`anchor_line`, `anchor_line_end`).** Both prompts ask each voice for the head-file line the finding
  sits on (`anchor_line`) and, for a range, its last line (`anchor_line_end`), beside the symbol `anchor` and
  `anchor_type`. The symbol anchor stays the stable reference and stays required for high-severity findings: the
  anchor check, `anchor_stability` and the hallucination filter key on `anchor` alone. The normaliser keeps a line only
  as a whole number from 1 to 10,000,000, and an end only beside a kept start and at least it; any other value is
  dropped silently, never a rejection or a repair hop. A finding with no line is unchanged. Graders (the eval harness's
  envelope reduction) read `anchor_line` with the anchor's file as `path:line[-end]`; read them as a pointer, never as
  a replacement for the symbol.
- **Budget scaling (`budget_scale`, `budget_cents_max`).** `flatline_protocol.<code_review|security_audit>.budget_scale`
  is `fixed` (the default; an absent key is the shipped gate, byte for byte) or `diff`: the budget becomes
  `min(max(budget_cents, ceil(estimate × 1.2)), budget_cents_max)` (`budget_cents_max` default 600), where the estimate
  is the gate's own pre-dispatch estimate over the planned voices. An estimate above that budget still refuses (exit 4,
  `status: budget_exceeded`, `reason: budget`). A malformed scale or maximum is said and `fixed` applies. When the key is
  written, the envelope's metadata carries `budget_scale`, `budget_cents_effective` and `budget_cents_max`. The eval
  harness writes `diff` for both gates in its sandbox config; the shipped default stays `fixed`.
=====RUBRICS
# Audit Rubrics

Structured evaluation rubrics for each audit category. Use these to score findings consistently.

## How to Use

1. For each dimension, assess the codebase against the criteria
2. Assign score 1-5 based on the rubric
3. Record reasoning trace explaining the score
4. Calculate category average for overall health

---

## Security Rubrics

### SEC-IV: Input Validation
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | All inputs validated, sanitized, and typed. Allowlist approach used. Schema validation on APIs. |
| 4 | Most inputs validated with minor gaps. Edge cases may lack validation. |
| 3 | Basic validation present but incomplete. Some injection risks remain. |
| 2 | Minimal validation. Clear injection vulnerabilities exist. |
| 1 | No input validation. User input flows directly to sensitive operations. |

### SEC-AZ: Authorization
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | RBAC/ABAC properly implemented. All routes protected. Least privilege enforced. |
| 4 | Authorization present with minor gaps (some routes missing checks). |
| 3 | Basic auth checks but inconsistent. Privilege escalation may be possible. |
| 2 | Weak authorization. Easy bypass or missing on critical routes. |
| 1 | No authorization or completely broken access control. |

### SEC-CI: Confidentiality/Integrity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Encryption at rest and in transit. Proper key management. Data classified and protected. |
| 4 | Good encryption with minor gaps. Some sensitive data handling could improve. |
| 3 | Basic encryption but inconsistent. Some data exposure risks. |
| 2 | Weak or missing encryption. Sensitive data partially exposed. |
| 1 | No encryption. Sensitive data in plaintext. Secrets in code. |

### SEC-IN: Injection Prevention
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Parameterized queries everywhere. No string concatenation in queries. ORM used safely. |
| 4 | Mostly safe with minor gaps in edge cases. |
| 3 | Mixed usage. Some queries parameterized, others vulnerable. |
| 2 | Frequent string concatenation in queries. Clear SQL/NoSQL injection paths. |
| 1 | Pervasive injection vulnerabilities. Eval/exec with user input. |

### SEC-AV: Availability/Resilience
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Rate limiting, circuit breakers, graceful degradation. DoS protection in place. |
| 4 | Good availability measures with minor gaps. |
| 3 | Basic rate limiting but incomplete. Some DoS vectors remain. |
| 2 | Minimal protection. Resource exhaustion possible. |
| 1 | No availability protection. Trivial DoS attacks possible. |

---

## Architecture Rubrics

### ARCH-MO: Modularity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Clear separation of concerns. Well-defined interfaces. Easy to modify/extend. |
| 4 | Good modularity with minor coupling issues. |
| 3 | Some modularity but tight coupling in places. |
| 2 | Poor separation. Components heavily interdependent. |
| 1 | Monolithic. No clear boundaries. |

### ARCH-SC: Scalability
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Horizontally
